items.title: Don Smedley and Tom Stagg Interview, 1969-10-03
items.q: Alvin Elkhorn came with Jimmy Archie, Donnell Howard, Elton Pennell again, Saif Frazier and Pops Foster. This was the last tour that Donnell Howard was to make... ctx.x: My... I first became interested in traditional style jazz while I was still at school. I was born in 1938. This was in about 1948, 49. The first record I ever bought was Louis Armstrong's Basin Street Blues, which I bought second hand at some ridiculous price of about eight shillings at that time, was a hell of a lot of money. I was doing a paper round and had seen this record in a post office, and had saved for about four weeks to buy this record, and hoping it hadn't gone. I used to go down and look at this…

Graham Russell and a girl, Ray Whittrick, decided to form a Bunk Johnson Appreciation Society, and they were holding once a month meetings in a pub, the Porcupine, just off Charing Cross Road in London. I joined this with my brother at that time, who was beginning to play a little bit of banjo, and we joined it, and the first meeting we ever went to must have been in late 1958, when Graham Russell came out of the Air Force.
